physics-killer-03.material: Object wey get mass $2\,\mathrm{kg}$ slide from rest from height $4\,\mathrm{m}$ for curved surface wey no get friction, pass through rough section for horizontal surface (length $5\,\mathrm{m}$, di size of friction force wey dey act on di object na constant $11\,\mathrm{N}$), and then climb di right slope wey no get friction. Take $g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$ and ignore air resistance. Which one correctly match, in order, di thermal energy $Q$ wey dey produce for di rough section and di maximum height wey e climb for di right slope?
physics-killer-03.thinking.0: Work and conversion between mechanical energies (Inquiry)
physics-killer-03.s.s1.prompt: Object wey get mass $2\,\mathrm{kg}$ slide from rest from height $4\,\mathrm{m}$ for curved surface wey no get friction, pass through rough section for horizontal surface (length $5\,\mathrm{m}$, di size of friction force wey dey act on di object na constant $11\,\mathrm{N}$), and then climb di right slope wey no get friction. Take $g=10\,\mathrm{m/s^2}$ and ignore air resistance. Which one correctly match, in order, di thermal energy $Q$ wey dey produce for di rough section and di maximum height wey e climb for di right slope?
physics-killer-03.s.s1.explain: Di initial mechanical energy $E_0=mgh_0=2\cdot10\cdot4=80\,\mathrm{J}$. For di rough section $Q=fs=11\cdot5=55\,\mathrm{J}$ turn heat, so di remaining mechanical energy na $80-55=25\,\mathrm{J}$. Di right slope no get friction, so from $25=mgh$ to $h=\dfrac{25}{2\cdot10}=1.25\,\mathrm{m}$. If you ignore friction and assume e climb reach $4\,\mathrm{m}$ na wrong answer ②, if you mistake di remaining energy $25\,\mathrm{J}$ as heat na wrong answer ③, and if you use $mgh$ instead of $\frac12mgh$ e go be $2.5\,\mathrm{m}$ (wrong answer ④).
